objective: Scheduling: how kube-scheduler filters and scores nodes using resource requests, node selectors and affinity, taints and tolerations, and topology spread, and what leaves a Pod Pending
secondaryObjectives: Scheduling: resource requests and limits, QoS classes, and how the scheduler and kubelet treat CPU and memory differently

sources.cite: Kubernetes documentation, Scheduling, Preemption and Eviction (print view)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: kube-scheduler filters nodes (for example, enough resources for the Pod's requests) and scores the rest; with no feasible node the Pod stays unscheduled; nodeSelector schedules only onto nodes with every listed label.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: a NoSchedule taint keeps Pods without a matching toleration off the node; tolerations allow but do not guarantee scheduling onto tainted nodes.

sources.cite: Kubernetes documentation, Pod Quality of Service Classes
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: a Pod with no requests or limits is BestEffort and is evicted first under node pressure.
The organization, the systems and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You support the development teams at Pennant Learning, a fictional education company. Three workloads went Pending after this morning's releases.
handover: The cluster has 3 general nodes (8 CPU each) and 3 GPU nodes tainted gpu=true:NoSchedule.
Nodes carry the label zone=eu-west-1a or zone=eu-west-1b.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: a batch job fills a node's memory; the kubelet evicts the BestEffort web Pods first and the site drops.
Check-in 3: web and batch Pods fill the GPU nodes; trainer is Pending again and GPU spend triples.
Check-in 4: a storage workload trusts the zone label and attaches volumes from the wrong zone; it fails to start.

requestsPrompt.title: Requests that do not fit
requestsPrompt.context: Six web replicas request 4 CPU each; they use about 0.3.

choices.label: Set web's CPU request to 500m from measured use, keeping a memory request and limit
choices.feedback: The scheduler filters nodes by the Pod's requests; oversized requests leave Pods Pending on idle nodes.

choices.label: Add two more general nodes
choices.feedback: It works, but pays for capacity the requests only pretend to need.

choices.label: Remove all requests and limits from web
choices.feedback: Web schedules anywhere, but BestEffort Pods are evicted first under pressure.

gpuPrompt.title: A GPU job that can't land
gpuPrompt.context: trainer selects gpu=true nodes, which are tainted.

choices.label: Add a toleration for gpu=true:NoSchedule and keep the nodeSelector, so trainer can land on GPU nodes and only there

effects.log: trainer schedules on a GPU node.

choices.feedback: A taint repels Pods without a matching toleration; the toleration allows, and the selector requires, the GPU nodes.

choices.label: Add the toleration and drop the nodeSelector
choices.feedback: A toleration allows GPU nodes but does not require them; trainer may land on a CPU node and fail.

choices.label: Remove the taint from the GPU nodes
choices.feedback: Every workload can now land on the expensive GPU nodes.

selectorPrompt.title: A selector nothing matches
selectorPrompt.context: reports selects zone=eu-west-1x; nodes are in 1a and 1b.

choices.label: Check node labels and fix reports' selector to zone=eu-west-1a, where its data must stay
choices.feedback: nodeSelector schedules only onto nodes with every listed label; a typo matches nothing.

choices.label: Delete the nodeSelector
choices.feedback: It runs, but may land in 1b, against the data placement rule.

choices.label: Label two nodes zone=eu-west-1x to match
choices.feedback: Node labels now lie; other workloads relying on zone labels misplace.

parts.label: Requests and taints

parts.modelAnswer: web's requests now match use, so it fits; trainer tolerates the GPU taint and still selects GPU nodes.

parts.label: Selectors
parts.modelAnswer: reports selected a zone that does not exist; it now selects eu-west-1a.

scoring.modelReasoning: kube-scheduler filters nodes by the Pod's resource requests, node selectors and taints, then scores the rest; with no feasible node the Pod stays Pending. Size requests from use, pair tolerations with selectors for dedicated nodes, and fix selectors rather than node labels.
